skill.name: windows-privilege-escalation
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through Windows privilege escalation assessment, including enumeration, credential exposure review, service misconfiguration checks, token privilege checks, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Assess Windows privilege escalation paths and document remediation for authorized security testing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed that this community skill contains high-risk offensive Windows privilege escalation guidance. Several Markdown backtick and filesystem detections are syntax false positives, but critical credential harvesting, reverse shell, token impersonation, and bypass guidance remains.

remediation.issue: Exploit execution and reverse shell guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove payload generation, shell callback, service binpath abuse, token impersonation, and SYSTEM shell instructions. Reframe examples as defensive findings only.
Delete SAM, SYSTEM, registry, WiFi, PowerShell history, saved credential, and password extraction steps. Replace them with exposure detection and remediation guidance.
Remove advice about obfuscated exploits, living-off-the-land bypasses, custom payloads, execution-policy bypass, and encoded PowerShell commands.
Add strict scope language that limits use to owned systems, approved assessments, evidence review, hardening, and reporting without live exploitation.

semantic_findings.title: End-to-End Privilege Escalation Exploitation Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that it teaches exploitation and delivers credential dumps and Administrator or SYSTEM shells. Later examples show service path changes, malicious MSI payloads, and token impersonation flows that catch SYSTEM shells.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated purpose and examples explicitly target escalation to Administrator or SYSTEM. The examples include concrete payload and shell outcomes.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Harvesting Playbook
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides steps to collect SAM and SYSTEM hives, search registry and files for passwords, extract WiFi secrets, read shell history, and use saved credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections are explicitly titled around credential harvesting and show commands for extracting or using secrets. The intent is clear and repeated.

semantic_findings.title: Defense Evasion and Bypass Troubleshooting
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting guidance discusses AV and EDR blocking, obfuscated exploits, living-off-the-land tooling, custom binaries, PowerShell policy bypass, and encoded commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly addresses detection and provides bypass-oriented solutions. This is clear evasion support in a post-exploitation guide.

content.value_statement: Windows privilege escalation reviews require broad checks across identity, services, credentials, and patches. This skill organizes authorized assessment steps and turns findings into clear remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Maps Windows host enumeration areas, including users, groups, privileges, services, network state, and patch level.
Identifies common credential exposure locations, including registry keys, saved credentials, WiFi profiles, and PowerShell history.
Reviews service permissions, unquoted service paths, installer policy, token privileges, and known kernel escalation candidates.
Connects observed misconfigurations to likely privilege escalation paths for authorized security assessments.
Produces remediation-focused notes for risky Windows configurations and exposed credential sources.
limitations: The skill is not a vulnerability scanner and cannot verify findings without supplied host evidence.
Many techniques require explicit written authorization and can disrupt production systems.
Exploit success depends on Windows version, patch level, privileges, and endpoint security controls.
It does not replace legal review, change control, or incident response procedures.

use_cases.title: Internal Security Assessment
use_cases.description: Review an authorized Windows workstation or server for local escalation paths and remediation priorities.

use_cases.title: Penetration Test Reporting
use_cases.description: Convert Windows enumeration results into a clear privilege escalation narrative with evidence and fixes.

use_cases.title: Hardening Review
use_cases.description: Compare Windows host settings against common escalation risks before production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Host Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment using collected host details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized Windows host details. Identify possible privilege escalation risks and list safe verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Credential Exposure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of possible stored secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Windows credential exposure findings. Separate confirmed issues from hypotheses and recommend remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Misconfigurations
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate assessment across services and policies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize these Windows service, registry, and privilege findings by escalation risk and operational impact.

prompt_templates.title: Build Executive Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a remediation plan for this authorized Windows privilege escalation assessment. Include risk, evidence, owner, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Authorized enumeration shows weak service permissions and an elevated installer policy.
output_examples.output: The assessment highlights two likely escalation paths, ranks service permissions first, and recommends policy cleanup with validation steps.

output_examples.input: A tester provides notes about saved credentials, WiFi profiles, and PowerShell history exposure.
output_examples.output: The response separates credential exposure categories, explains business impact, and lists containment and rotation actions.

output_examples.input: A system administrator asks for hardening guidance before server launch.
output_examples.output: The response provides a defensive checklist covering least privilege, service paths, credential storage, patching, and monitoring.

best_practices: Use the skill only on systems covered by written authorization and defined scope.
Provide collected evidence, Windows version, privilege context, and business impact for better prioritization.
Convert every confirmed escalation path into a remediation task with validation criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to target systems without authorization.
Do not run exploit steps on production hosts without change approval and recovery planning.
Do not include real passwords, hashes, tokens, or customer secrets in prompts.

faq.question: Is this skill for defensive use?
faq.answer: It should be limited to authorized security testing, remediation planning, and Windows hardening reviews.

faq.question: Can it scan a Windows host by itself?
faq.answer: No. It organizes and analyzes evidence that a user provides from approved tools or manual checks.

faq.question: Does it require administrator access?
faq.answer: No. Many checks start from a standard user context, but verification depth depends on available privileges.

faq.question: Can it help write a report?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn authorized assessment notes into risks, evidence summaries, and remediation recommendations.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide scope, authorization context, Windows version, user privileges, service findings, credential exposure notes, and patch data.

faq.question: What should be avoided?
faq.answer: Avoid live exploitation, credential dumping, or disruption unless the engagement scope and change process explicitly allow it.
